findings.where: Whole page at desktop width: the text column (intro, Surf, Vibe, What to look for) against the Good for chip rows and the coming-soon block
findings.fault: The page has no single content width. The text sits in a narrow column, about 520 px wide, hard against the left edge. The chip rows stop about 440 px further right. The coming-soon block runs the full 1052 px container but keeps its text in the left half, so the right half is an empty band of red. Three right edges never line up (continuity). The first screen is mostly blank sand on the right, which makes the page look half-built rather than set as a deliberate editorial column.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker planning on a laptop sees a lopsided page with a dead right half and a box that seems to be missing its content. That cuts against the brand's 'effortless' and crafted first feeling, and makes a pre-launch guide look unfinished.

findings.where: Section headings down the guide: 'Surf', 'Vibe', 'Good for', 'What to look for'
findings.fault: Four parallel sections get three different heading treatments. 'Surf' and 'Good for' are plain h2s. 'Vibe' is italic, turquoise and underlined, so it looks like a link. 'What to look for' is a small tracked uppercase label. Similarity breaks: a reader can't tell these are equal sections. The section the brief cares about most, what to look for in a Canggu hostel, has the weakest heading on the page and reads like a caption to the chips above it.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker skimming for 'what should I look for' misses that section or takes it for a footnote. Someone skimming the headings can't find the page's outline, and 'Vibe' looks clickable when it isn't.

findings.where: 'Good for' chip cloud (12 pills), desktop and phone
findings.fault: On a squint, the 12 saturated pills, each with a contrasting border, beat everything else on the page, including the title and the opening paragraph. They are the busiest block on the page, sitting mid-page with nothing to say why they deserve that weight. Their colours rotate through five hues with no meaning, so similarity invents groups that don't exist (the pink pills look like one category, the teal ones like another).
findings.who_objects: A visitor's eye lands on a tag cloud of loose labels instead of the guide's substance and tries to decode a colour key that isn't there. That goes against the brand's rule that colour carries information.

findings.fault: The footer links wrap after 'How we rank', which leaves a '·' separator hanging at the end of the first line and none at the start of the second, so the row reads as broken.
findings.who_objects: A phone visitor checking who runs the site sees a sloppy wrap in the trust zone. Few would notice.
